description: An empty batting hand means unknown: those players (and NULL-hand players) are removed before anything is computed.

c.request: For each player in the postseason batting data (matched to `player` on `player_id`), take their average postseason doubles per record, ignoring missing values, along with their batting hand. Divide it by the overall average of these per-player averages to get a relative index. Then show how far each player's index sits above the average index for their batting hand. Give the top 10 players by that gap, largest first (missing last), with player id, batting hand, average doubles, index, and the gap, unrounded. An empty batting hand means unknown: those players (and NULL-hand players) are removed before anything is computed.
c.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        bp.player_id,
        p.bats AS batting_hand,
        AVG(bp.double) AS avg_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS bp
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL
      AND p.bats <> ''
    GROUP BY bp.player_id, p.bats
), indexed_players AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        batting_hand,
        avg_doubles,
        avg_doubles / AVG(avg_doubles) OVER () AS index
    FROM player_averages
)
SELECT
    player_id,
    batting_hand,
    avg_doubles,
    index,
    index - AVG(index) OVER (PARTITION BY batting_hand) AS gap
FROM indexed_players
ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

a.request: Matching postseason batting records to players on `player_id`, work out each player's average postseason doubles per record (ignoring missing values), grouped by player and batting hand (`player.bats`). Turn that into a relative index by dividing it by the overall average of these per-player averages. Then compare each player's index with the average index of players who have the same batting hand. List the 10 players whose index is furthest above their batting-hand average. Show the player id, batting hand, average doubles, index, and index minus the hand average, sorted by that difference from highest to lowest (missing values last), unrounded. Leave out players whose batting hand is empty or missing (NULL) entirely, including from the overall average.
a.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        p.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(bp.double) AS average_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS bp
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id
    WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL
      AND p.bats <> ''
    GROUP BY p.player_id, p.bats
),
indexed AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        average_doubles / AVG(average_doubles) OVER () AS index_value
    FROM player_averages
),
compared AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        average_doubles,
        index_value,
        index_value - AVG(index_value) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS difference
    FROM indexed
)
SELECT
    player_id,
    bats,
    average_doubles,
    index_value,
    difference
FROM compared
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10

b.request: Exclude players whose batting hand is empty or NULL before any calculations; for each remaining player with postseason batting records, compute the average of non-NULL postseason doubles per record, then divide by the overall average of those player-level averages to get an index. Subtract the average index among players with the same batting hand from each player’s index, and return the 10 largest gaps first, placing missing gaps last, with player ID, batting hand, average doubles, index, and gap, all unrounded
b.sql:
WITH eligible_players AS (
    SELECT player_id, bats
    FROM player
    WHERE bats IS NOT NULL AND bats <> ''
), player_averages AS (
    SELECT ep.player_id, ep.bats, AVG(bp.double) AS average_doubles
    FROM eligible_players ep
    JOIN batting_postseason bp ON bp.player_id = ep.player_id
    GROUP BY ep.player_id, ep.bats
), indexed_players AS (
    SELECT player_id, bats, average_doubles,
           average_doubles / NULLIF(AVG(average_doubles) OVER (), 0) AS idx
    FROM player_averages
), with_gaps AS (
    SELECT player_id, bats, average_doubles, idx,
           idx - AVG(idx) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
    FROM indexed_players
)
SELECT player_id, bats, average_doubles, idx AS index, gap
FROM with_gaps
ORDER BY CASE WHEN gap IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, gap DESC
LIMIT 10;

d.request: For each player in the postseason batting data, matched to `player` by `player_id`, calculate their average postseason doubles per record, ignoring missing values. Exclude players whose batting hand is empty or NULL before doing any calculations. Divide each remaining player’s average by the overall average of these per-player averages to get a relative index, then subtract the average index for that player’s batting hand to find the gap. Return the 10 players with the largest gaps first, with missing gaps last. Include player ID, batting hand, average doubles, index, and gap, without rounding.
d.sql:
WITH player_averages AS (
    SELECT
        b.player_id,
        p.bats,
        AVG(b.double) AS avg_doubles
    FROM batting_postseason AS b
    JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = b.player_id
    WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL
      AND p.bats <> ''
    GROUP BY b.player_id, p.bats
),
indexed AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        avg_doubles,
        avg_doubles / AVG(avg_doubles) OVER () AS player_index
    FROM player_averages
),
with_gaps AS (
    SELECT
        player_id,
        bats,
        avg_doubles,
        player_index,
        player_index - AVG(player_index) OVER (PARTITION BY bats) AS gap
    FROM indexed
)
SELECT player_id, bats, avg_doubles, player_index, gap
FROM with_gaps
ORDER BY gap DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
